description: We are young innovators interested in using technology and Earth observation data to address environmental challenges in Uganda. Our interests and skills include software development, GIS, climate science and data visualisation. Through H2O StressX Ug, we aim to make water-stress information easier to understand and use. We welcome participants with skills in hydrology, remote sensing, programming, UI/UX design and environmental research.
summary:
H2O StressX Ug is an interactive geospatial platform developed to help people understand water stress and changing environmental conditions across Uganda using NASA Earth observation data.

The platform brings rainfall, temperature and modelled land wetness information into an accessible map-based interface. Users can explore different locations, examine environmental indicators and understand how variations in rainfall and temperature may influence water availability.

Water stress affects agriculture, livelihoods and environmental planning, yet satellite-based information is often difficult for ordinary people to interpret. H2O StressX Ug addresses this gap by presenting environmental observations through interactive maps, understandable charts and practical explanations.

The project is designed for farmers, students, researchers and local planners who need accessible information about changing water-related conditions.

By making NASA environmental data easier to explore, H2O StressX Ug aims to improve water-stress awareness, support informed planning and encourage better understanding of the environmental factors affecting water resources in Uganda.
details:
H2O StressX Ug

Understanding Water Stress Through NASA Earth Observation Data

The Problem

Water availability is essential for agriculture, food security, environmental management and livelihoods across Uganda. Many communities depend on seasonal rainfall, making them vulnerable to prolonged dry conditions and changes in rainfall patterns.

However, understanding water stress requires more than simply observing whether it has rained. Temperature, soil conditions, seasonal changes and other environmental factors can influence water availability.

NASA provides valuable environmental datasets, but these are often presented in formats that require technical knowledge to interpret.

We developed H2O StressX Ug to make this information easier to explore and understand.

Our Solution

H2O StressX Ug is an interactive web-based geospatial platform that helps users examine environmental conditions associated with water stress across Uganda.

The application combines environmental observations with geographical visualisation, allowing users to explore locations and examine indicators such as precipitation, temperature and modelled root-zone wetness.

Rather than presenting raw scientific data alone, the platform communicates environmental conditions through maps, charts and understandable explanations.

How the Platform Works

1. Interactive Map

Users explore Uganda through a geographical interface and select locations of interest.

2. NASA Environmental Data

The platform uses NASA POWER environmental information to examine rainfall, temperature and available modelled land wetness indicators.

3. Environmental Visualisation

Environmental data is presented through charts and geographical displays, making it easier to examine changing conditions.

4. Water-Stress Awareness

Users can explore how rainfall variability, temperature and land wetness may relate to water-stress conditions.

5. Data Export

Available environmental information can be downloaded in CSV format for further examination.

6. Practical Guidance

The platform provides general environmental recommendations to support water-stress awareness and informed planning.

Technologies Used

H2O StressX Ug was developed using:

  • Next.js for the web application and server-side functionality.
  • React for the interactive user interface.
  • TypeScript for application development.
  • Tailwind CSS for responsive design.
  • React Leaflet and Leaflet for geographical visualisation.
  • NASA POWER for environmental observations and modelled indicators.
  • CSV export for downloading environmental information.

What Makes Our Project Innovative?

H2O StressX Ug focuses on transforming scientific environmental data into information that people can understand.

The project combines NASA Earth observation resources, interactive geographical exploration and accessible visualisations within a single platform focused on Uganda.

Its main innovation is the way it connects environmental observations with locations, making water-related information easier to explore without requiring advanced technical knowledge.

Intended Impact

Farmers: Improve awareness of environmental conditions that may influence agricultural activities.

Students and Educators: Provide an interactive way to explore rainfall, temperature and water-related environmental concepts.

Researchers: Support the exploration of environmental indicators through a geographical interface.

Local Planners: Provide additional environmental context for discussions about water availability and climate variability.

Scientific Considerations

Environmental observations and modelled indicators provide useful regional information but cannot directly determine water availability at every individual farm or household.

H2O StressX Ug is intended as an exploratory environmental information platform rather than an operational drought forecasting system.

The current implementation does not include validated direct SMAP soil moisture integration, MODIS vegetation index integration or a complete nationwide water-stress raster.

Future Development

Future improvements may include additional satellite datasets, historical comparisons, improved water-stress assessment methods, local-language accessibility and expanded geographical coverage.

Conclusion

H2O StressX Ug makes NASA environmental information more accessible through an interactive geospatial platform focused on Uganda.

By bringing together rainfall, temperature and land wetness indicators, the project aims to improve water-stress awareness and support informed environmental decisions.
